newsitem.title: USA: Sour crude prices shoot higher in stormy U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Sour crude prices shoot higher in stormy U.S. Gulf.

text.p: Cash crude grade barrels continued to gain strength Tuesday afternoon, attracting deals at more expensive prices for both sweet and sour parcels.
Outright July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 20 cents firmer at $19.25-35 a barrel, figuring in an eight cents premium to the NYMEX screen off Exchange for Physicals.
Traders said violent storms in the Houston area gave pause to trading activity, but the momentum for stronger grade prices remained undeterred.

The feature of the session has centered on large amounts of West Texas Sour/Midland changing hands at only a $1.25 under July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, marking a 25 cents gain from late Monday.
At the same time, sweet grades trimmed discounts as well, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James dealt as firm as two cents under the benchmark.
Traders said refiners picking-up ratable barrels pumped life into what has been a static and dead trading range in recent weeks.
"With the July/August spread not showing much life, LLS has become a fairly good value," said a cash dealer in Texas.

Supply worries and concerns over when Iraqi crude will return to market supported North Sea Brent. Wet Brent, a key competitor for LLS in the U.S. Gulf, moved at August Brent -60 cents for a June 26-28 loader, a shade weaker than Monday.
The sour grade performance came mainly on a heavy volume deal with a refiner.
Other action saw Eugene Island barrels moved at a $1.80 under WTI/Cushing and WTI/Cushing Postings Plus at $1.85 and $1.90.
